en.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Shatters Records With Astonishing $145M Second Weekend
en.summary: The latest webslinger adventure continues its historic run, pulling in a colossal $145 million in its second weekend. This monumental haul cements its place among the all-time box office greats.
en.body:
Few films land with the seismic impact of a major superhero tentpole, and **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is proving to be no exception. In a stunning display of box office dominance, the latest outing for Tom Holland's Peter Parker has snagged an incredible $145 million in its second weekend of release. This phenomenal figure not only cements its status as a cultural phenomenon but also secures its place in the history books, boasting the third-best second weekend haul of all time.

This isn't just about a strong sophomore frame, though. The film has been on a record-breaking tear since its debut. It previously achieved the fastest climb to $500 million domestically, surpassing even the mighty **Avengers: Endgame** by a full day. With its latest weekend earnings, the domestic total for **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** now stands at a staggering $655.1 million, making it the highest-grossing film after just 10 days in theaters. This level of sustained audience engagement is a testament to the film's broad appeal, drawing in fans worldwide who are clearly captivated by this iteration of the beloved character.

## A New Day at the Box Office

Against a slate of newcomers including **One Night Only**, **Super Troopers 3**, and **Ice Cream Man**, **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** refused to cede its top spot. The film's ability to maintain such momentum, experiencing only a 60% drop from its opening weekend – a hold comparable to **Avengers: Endgame** – speaks volumes about its widespread appeal. This resilience is particularly noteworthy in a crowded marketplace, proving that a well-executed blockbuster can continue to dominate long after its initial release. The film's per-screen average of $32,316 from 4,487 screens further underscores its massive draw.

Meanwhile, A24's **Tony**, a biographical drama about a young Anthony Bourdain starring Dominic Sessa, opened to a promising $400,000 on just six screens. While a fraction of **Spider-Man**'s numbers, its critical acclaim, evidenced by a 95% score on Rotten Tomatoes, highlights a different kind of cinematic success, one focused on critical darling status and unique storytelling.

## The Web Continues to Grow

For the legions of fans who have flocked to theaters, **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** represents more than just a movie; it's a shared cultural event. The record-breaking numbers are a clear indicator of the community's passionate engagement with the Marvel Cinematic Universe and the specific journey of Peter Parker. This sustained box office success fuels anticipation for future installments and solidifies the film's place as a modern classic. The conversations happening online and offline about the film’s twists, turns, and emotional beats are a testament to its impact on its audience.

## What's Next for the Wall-Crawler

With its current trajectory, **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is poised to climb even higher on the all-time box office charts. Future weeks will reveal if it can challenge for an even more elite spot in cinematic history. Fans will undoubtedly continue to flock to theaters to witness this web-slinging phenomenon.

content_raw: Tom Holland's blockbuster delivers one of the top sophomore frames in history while competing with newcomers 'One Night Only,' 'Super Troopers 3' and 'Ice Cream Man.'
